verdict.summary: Creating a public connection and authorizing it with your own account is self-serve in the Notion Developer portal with no review. Only listing the connection on the Notion Marketplace requires a Notion security review, and Notion does not publish a turnaround time for it. Installation scope is fixed at creation, so choose it before you start.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 1-2 hours for a working own-account connection and Composio hookup; listing preparation and submission add more, and the review wait is outside your control.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Under 1 hour (internal connection, then convert to public, then paste client ID and secret into Composio)
verdict.approval_wait: None for own-account or Selected-workspaces use. Marketplace listing review: no turnaround documented by Notion.

gates.name: Public connection, own account (created as internal, then converted to public)
gates.unlocks: You can create the connection, set its redirect URI and capabilities, paste its credentials into Composio, and authorize it with your own Notion account.
limits: Every new connection starts as internal; you must create an internal connection first and then convert it to public (f5).
Any Notion member can build connections, not only Workspace Owners (f3).

gates.name: Public connection with Selected workspaces only
gates.unlocks: Other users in the workspaces you select at creation can authorize the connection. Each authorizing user gets their own token scoped to their workspace. No allowlist of test users was documented.
limits: Installation scope is set at creation (Any workspace or Selected workspaces only) and cannot be changed afterward (f7, f8).
Default rate limit is 3 requests per second per integration per workspace, from a community source (f28).
No install-count cap or user limit for unlisted public connections was found (f27).
Users must re-authenticate if the connection's capabilities change (f25).
gates.time_to_reach: Same session as Gate 1; no Notion review

gates.name: Public connection listed on the Notion Marketplace (Any workspace scope)
gates.unlocks: Any Notion workspace can install the connection from the Marketplace after Notion approves the listing.
limits: Only public connections with Any workspace scope can be listed (f11).
Every listing submission is reviewed by the Notion team; feedback may require changes and resubmission (f12, f13).
Connections can be rejected for various reasons, including brand or trademark issues (f14).
Higher rate limits (up to 100 requests/second) can be requested from Notion sales for Business or Enterprise workspaces, per community sources (f29).
gates.time_to_reach: Unknown. Build time plus a Notion security review; no turnaround documented.

steps.title: Open the Developer portal and confirm access
steps.detail: Sign in to Notion and open app.notion.com/developers in a browser with JavaScript enabled, since the portal does not render without it. Any workspace member can create connections, so you do not need to be a Workspace Owner.
gotchas: The portal is a JavaScript app; a blank page usually means JavaScript is disabled.

steps.title: Create an internal connection, then convert it to public
steps.detail: Create a new connection in the Developer portal. Every connection starts as internal, so you must create it as internal first, then convert it to a public connection. Use the portal's current labels; this guide does not give exact menu names for these actions.
gotchas: You cannot create a public connection directly; the internal-first step is required.

steps.title: Choose the installation scope at creation
steps.detail: Pick Any workspace if you may later list on the Marketplace, or Selected workspaces only if you want installs limited to workspaces you name. This choice is permanent and cannot be changed after the connection is created.

values.label: Installation scope options
values.value: Any workspace (Marketplace-eligible) or Selected workspaces only (not Marketplace-eligible)

gotchas: If you pick Selected workspaces, the connection can never be listed on the Marketplace, and the docs do not say whether it can later be widened.
Pick Any workspace now if there is any chance you will want a listing.

steps.title: Set the Redirect URI in the OAuth configuration section
steps.detail: In the connection form, fill in the OAuth configuration section with the redirect URI. The URI must match exactly what Composio sends in the token request. It cannot contain URL fragments, relative paths, wildcards, or a public IP address.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Copy the URL exactly, including the scheme and path; a mismatch fails the token exchange.
Notion's token request requires redirect_uri in most cases.

steps.title: Select the minimum capabilities
steps.detail: Draft the capability list for your use case: content read, update and insert, plus user information level (none, without email addresses, or with email addresses). Request only what the app needs, because fewer capabilities make a workspace admin more likely to install the connection. An agent can draft this list; you confirm it in the portal.

values.label: Content capabilities
values.value: read, update, insert (select only what you need)

values.label: User information levels
values.value: No user information; User information without email addresses; User information with email addresses

gotchas: Changing capabilities later forces existing users to re-authenticate.
Notion has no granular OAuth scopes; the Composio default scope list is empty for this reason.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret into Composio
steps.detail: From the connection's credentials in the Developer portal, copy the OAuth client ID and client secret. In your Composio auth config for the notion toolkit, paste them in and save. Composio's managed Notion app is available, but a public connection of your own is needed if you want your own branding or install and rate profile.
gotchas: Keep the client secret out of source control; it is shown once in the portal flow and can be rotated if lost, but the docs captured here do not say how.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start the OAuth flow from Composio (or the authorize URL) and sign in with your own Notion account. An agent can run this check and report whether the redirect and token exchange succeed. Each authorizing user receives their own token, so repeat with a second account in another workspace to confirm.
gotchas: An invalid client_id did not return an OAuth error on the authorize endpoint; it redirected to Notion's install page, so errors may only appear in the web UI.
The token exchange uses HTTP Basic auth with the client ID and secret, which is how Composio performs it.

steps.title: Invite test installs and watch limits
steps.detail: Authorize the connection from one or two other users in workspaces you selected at creation. Check the Health tab in the Developer portal for the last 24 hours of API requests and any rate-limit warnings. Plan for the default limit of 3 requests per second per integration per workspace unless you have an approved increase.
gotchas: No test-user allowlist or install cap for unlisted public connections was documented, so verify limits in the portal before wider use.
The Health tab is reported by a third-party release tracker, not Notion's own docs.

steps.title: Decide whether to list on the Marketplace
steps.detail: Listing is optional; you can run a public connection without it. If you want a listing, it must be an Any workspace connection, which you cannot create retroactively from a Selected-workspaces connection. Decide this before building the listing, since it determines which connection you need.
gotchas: A listed connection must go through Notion's security review.

steps.title: Prepare listing assets and text
steps.detail: An agent can draft the listing name, description, category, and tags. You supply images and a logo, and link the public connection the listing belongs to. Check that the name and branding do not infringe third-party trademarks, since brand issues are a common rejection reason.

values.label: Required listing fields
values.value: Name, description, category and tags, images, logo, associated public connection

gotchas: Notion's FAQ says rejections include brand/trademark issues; the full list of rejection reasons was not captured.
Other listing requirements (such as privacy policy or support URL) were not captured; check the Listings dashboard before submitting.

steps.title: Submit the listing for review
steps.detail: In the Developer portal, go to Listings > Connections and submit the connection with its listing details. Notion's team reviews every submission, including a security review of the connection.
gotchas: Submission is a UI action only you can complete; it is not an API step.

steps.title: Wait for the Notion security review
steps.detail: Notion reviews the listing and may send feedback. Official docs do not give a turnaround time for connection listings; a figure of days to a couple of weeks found online refers to template Marketplace submissions, not OAuth connections.
gotchas: Do not plan around the 'days to a couple of weeks' figure; it is for template submissions.

steps.title: Address feedback and resubmit
steps.detail: If Notion requests changes, update the listing or connection as directed and resubmit from the same dashboard. Rejections may cite brand or trademark issues, so address those before resubmitting.
gotchas: A rejected listing does not block Gate 1 or Gate 2 use of the connection.

steps.title: Confirm the approved listing is live
steps.detail: Once approved, the connection appears in the Notion Marketplace and any workspace can install it. Re-check the Health tab for rate-limit warnings from the broader install base.
gotchas: Higher rate limits, up to 100 requests/second, can be requested from Notion sales for Business or Enterprise workspaces, per community sources.

requirements.detail: Workspace Owner status is not required to build a connection.
Create an internal connection, then convert it to public. Public connections cannot be created directly.
Register the Composio callback URL in the OAuth configuration section. No fragments, relative paths, wildcards, or public IP addresses.
Any workspace or Selected workspaces only. Cannot be changed afterward.
Fewer capabilities make workspace admin installs more likely. Capability changes force re-authentication.

requirements.item: Any workspace scope for Marketplace listing
requirements.detail: Only Any workspace public connections can be listed.
Public connections must pass a Notion security review before Marketplace listing. Not required for unlisted use.

requirements.item: Listing name, description, category, tags, images, logo, associated connection
requirements.detail: Required fields for a Marketplace listing.
Brand or trademark issues are among the stated rejection reasons.

scopes.scope: Notion has no granular OAuth scopes
scopes.effect: Access is set by connection capabilities, not scopes. The Composio default scope list is empty for this reason, so there is nothing to request in the OAuth consent step beyond the connection setup.
Together these determine which API endpoints the connection can call. Request only what you need.

scopes.scope: User information: none, without email addresses, with email addresses
scopes.effect: Email access is the broadest user-information level. Requesting it may reduce installs by workspace admins, per the minimum-capabilities guidance.
No separate sensitive or restricted tier with its own review was found. The Marketplace security review appears to be the only review step.

blockers.symptom: Cannot list the connection on the Marketplace; the listing option is unavailable or ineligible.
blockers.cause: The connection was created with Selected workspaces only. Installation scope cannot be changed after creation, and only Any workspace connections are eligible.
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with Any workspace scope if you want a listing. Do not assume the existing connection can be widened; the docs do not say.

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected or sent back with feedback.
blockers.cause: Notion reviews every listing and may reject connections for various reasons, including brand or trademark issues. The full list was not captured.
blockers.fix: Read the feedback, fix the flagged items (especially name, logo, and branding), and resubmit from Listings > Connections.

blockers.symptom: Requests are throttled or return rate-limit errors for an unapproved public connection.
blockers.cause: Unapproved public integrations keep the default limit of 3 requests per second per integration per workspace. Higher limits require approval.
blockers.fix: Reduce request rate and batch calls. For higher limits, Business or Enterprise workspaces can contact Notion sales (community-reported, up to 100 requests/second).
blockers.contact: Notion sales (contact form not captured in findings)

blockers.symptom: Cannot estimate when a Marketplace listing will be approved.
blockers.cause: No review turnaround time for connection listings is documented. The commonly cited 'days to a couple of weeks' figure is for template Marketplace submissions.
blockers.fix: Plan for an unknown review window. Ask Notion directly through the portal or support if the timeline matters for your launch.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Notion OAuth app to test quickly; it needs no Notion app of your own. Create your own public connection if you want your own branding, control over install scope, or your own rate profile. A Composio guide says a public Notion integration is required for its OAuth flow, so you will paste your client ID and secret into Composio either way. It was not verified whether Composio's managed app avoids Notion's review for end users, so do not assume it does.

open_questions: No review turnaround time for public connection Marketplace listings was found in official docs.
No install-count cap or user limit for unlisted public connections was found; rate-limit figures rely on third-party blogs.
Sensitive or restricted capability tiers were not found; Notion appears to gate review on Marketplace listing rather than on specific capabilities.
PKCE support and refresh-token expiry were not confirmed from official docs; a third-party catalog lists refresh support.
The full list of listing rejection reasons was not captured.
Whether Composio's managed Notion app avoids Notion's review for end users, versus a developer-owned public connection, was not verified.
Listing requirements beyond name, description, category, tags, images, logo, and associated connection (for example privacy policy or support URL) were not captured.
Whether a Selected-workspaces connection can later be widened to Any workspace is unknown; docs say scope cannot be changed after creation.
Several official pages (marketplace listing, authorization, public connections) were only partially retrieved; some details rely on search snippets.
Exact menu labels for creating an internal connection and converting it to public were not captured; the guide uses generic wording.
